title: The Cleansing of the Kaaba
subtitle: The Purification of the Interior, the Eternal Custody of Banu Shaybah, and Bilal's Historic Adhan
summary: Following the toppling of the outer idols, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ oversaw the complete cleansing of the interior of the Kaaba, commanding the removal of all images and pagan relics before stepping inside to pray. In a timeless testament to institutional justice, the Prophet summoned Uthman ibn Talha and returned the key of the sanctuary to Banu Shaybah as an eternal trust. Ascending the roof of the purified Kaaba, Bilal proclaimed the Adhan, marking the permanent restoration of monotheism.

sections.text: Purifying the Interior of the Sacred Sanctuary

While the outer courtyard had been cleared of the 360 idols surrounding the perimeter, the interior chamber of the Kaaba still contained pagan artwork, statues, and ritual artifacts introduced during centuries of pre-Islamic decadence. Among these were carved depictions of prophets holding divining arrows (azlam)—a pagan practice of fortune-telling abhorrent to monotheistic faith. Standing at the threshold, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ firmly refused to enter the sacred interior until every single pagan relic was completely removed.
In an authentic narration documented in Sahih al-Bukhari, Abdullah ibn Abbas reported:

إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمَّا قَدِمَ أَبَى أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْبَيْتَ وَفِيهِ الآلِهَةُ، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا فَأُخْرِجَتْ... ثُمَّ دَخَلَ فَكَبَّرَ فِي نَوَاحِي الْبَيْتِ، وَلَمْ يُصَلِّ فِيهِ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ
'When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, he refused to enter the House while there were idols within it; he ordered them removed and they were taken out... Then he entered, proclaimed the greatness of Allah in the corners of the House, and then came out.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 4288)

Seeing a depiction falsely attributing divination to Prophet Ibrahim and Ismail, the Prophet exclaimed with deep grief: 'May Allah destroy them! By Allah, they knew well that Ibrahim never practiced divination with arrows! Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was an upright Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.' He ordered water and lotus leaves, and the walls were thoroughly washed clean until every trace of idolatry was erased.

Once the purification was complete, the Prophet entered the Kaaba accompanied only by Usama ibn Zayd, Bilal ibn Rabah, and the hereditary key-bearer Uthman ibn Talha. The heavy wooden door was closed behind them for a period of private devotion. In an authentic narration in Sahih al-Bukhari, Abdullah ibn Umar later inquired of Bilal regarding the Prophet's prayer inside:

سَأَلْتُ بِلاَلاً: 'أَيْنَ صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم؟' قَالَ: 'بَيْنَ الْعَمُودَيْنِ تِلْقَاءَ وَجْهِهِ'
'I asked Bilal: 'Where did the Prophet ﷺ pray?' He replied: 'Between the two columns facing him.'' (Sahih al-Bukhari 505)

Inside the cool, fragrant interior of the sanctuary, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood between the two southern wooden pillars, offering two units of prayer in sublime gratitude, turning to each corner of the Kaaba to proclaim: 'Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar!'
The Return of the Key to Banu Shaybah

As the Prophet emerged from the Kaaba and stood at the elevated doorway, a vast sea of people filled the courtyard. Ali ibn Abi Talib and Al-Abbas approached, requesting that the custody of the Kaaba's key (al-sidanah) be combined with their existing hereditary privilege of providing water to the pilgrims (al-siqayah), thereby consolidating all sanctuary honors within the House of Hashim.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Uthman ibn Talha, the pre-Islamic key-bearer who had previously locked the Kaaba against the Prophet during the days of Makkan persecution. In fulfillment of the divine injunction in Surah An-Nisa—'Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due' (4:58)—the Prophet extended the key to Uthman and uttered words of immortal institutional justice:

خُذُوهَا يَا بَنِي طَلْحَةَ خَالِدَةً تَالِدَةً، لاَ يَنْزِعُهَا مِنْكُمْ إِلاَّ ظَالِمٌ
'Take it, O Banu Talha, as an everlasting and eternal trust; none shall take it from you except an oppressor!' (Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham)

This monumental act demonstrated that the conquest of Islam was not an acquisition of tribal spoils, but the establishment of an immutable rule of law and justice that respected legitimate historical rights.
Bilal's Adhan from the Roof of the Kaaba

As the midday sun reached its zenith, the Prophet commanded Bilal ibn Rabah to ascend to the very roof of the Kaaba. Standing upon the ancient stone cornice where idols had held sway for centuries, Bilal raised his hands to his ears and proclaimed the Adhan in his soaring, melodious voice. The words 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest) cascaded over the rooftops, rocky gorges, and surrounding hills of Makkah.

Tears flowed freely from the eyes of the believers. The very man who had been dragged across the scorched sands of Makkah with a boulder on his chest, whispering 'Ahad, Ahad' (One, One), was now proclaiming monotheism from the pinnacle of the sanctuary. The cleansing was complete: polytheism was eradicated, and the Kaaba returned forever to the worship of the One Creator.
